key_insight: The paper turns phase-field fracture for composite shells into a mechanism-resolved, operator-based framework where fibre, inter-fibre, and interaction damage channels are handled through an admissible constitutive operator rather than a single fixed energy law.
engineering_relevance: This enables more flexible and certifiable simulation of curved fibre-reinforced shells, improving predictive fracture modelling for cases where orientation, curvature, and through-thickness effects strongly influence failure.
method: Pulls the Green-Lagrange strain through the shell metric/Cholesky transform and resolves it into four orthogonal invariants with exact closure.
Implements tension-compression split, channel-wise degradation, plane-stress condensation, and consistent tangent directly in channel potentials and derivatives.
Defines six admissibility conditions plus a three-tier certification protocol for algebra, solver state, and training-data admission.
evidence_signal: Numerical tests on notched IM7/8552 shells in thin and curved regimes validate the discretisation and show that fibre orientation and curvature significantly affect damage patterns and load capacity.
watch_item: The framework depends on admissible operator conditions and positive residual stiffness for regular plane-stress condensation, so learned or custom operators still require careful certification.
paper_title: Mechanism-resolved phase-field fracture of composite shells with a certified admissible constitutive operator
